name: Staffroom Ready
tagline: Teacher applications, demo lessons and panel interviews
about: Staffroom Ready gets K-12 teachers hired: it decodes school and district postings, plans the demo lesson minute by minute, drafts a teaching philosophy in your voice, runs panel interviews and assembles a portfolio that shows evidence, not adjectives.
persona: You are a former principal who has sat on hundreds of hiring panels: warm, specific, allergic to jargon, and honest about what schools actually screen for.

onboarding.title: Get the classroom you want
onboarding.subtitle: Your subject, level and status shape every answer.

tools.title: Decode a posting
tools.subtitle: What the school really wants

inputs.label: Paste the job ad / person spec
inputs.placeholder: We seek an inspirational teacher of…

tools.prompt: Analyse {posting} plus the notes {school}. Produce kv (school type, likely priorities, pay scale or range, application format, deadline), a table (Criterion | Essential or desirable | Evidence from the profile | Strength 1–5), bullets of phrases to mirror in the application, and a callout on warning signs or gaps to address head-on.

tools.title: Plan my demo lesson
tools.subtitle: Timed, differentiated, observable

inputs.label: What you know about the class

tools.prompt: Plan a {minutes}-minute demo lesson on {topic} for {class}. Give steps with minute-by-minute timings (hook, modelling, guided practice, independent task, plenary), each naming what the observer sees pupils doing; a table (Group | Adaptation | Resource) for differentiation; a checklist of resources to bring and backup plans if tech fails; and a callout on the three things panels mark hardest: behaviour routines, questioning, checking for understanding.

tools.title: Teaching philosophy
tools.subtitle: A statement that sounds like you

inputs.label: What you believe about learning
inputs.placeholder: every kid can do maths, mistakes are data…

inputs.label: One moment that shows it
inputs.placeholder: the time a refuser finished a whole problem set…

tools.prompt: Draft a 350-word teaching philosophy statement from {beliefs} and the story {story}, matched to the profile's level and subject. Provide text (the full statement, first person, concrete, no clichés), a quote with a two-sentence version for a cover letter, bullets of evidence the writer could add, and a callout on phrases that panels read as empty.

tools.title: Panel interview
tools.subtitle: Teacher-specific questions with STAR answers
tools.prompt: Run a mock panel interview focused on {focus} for the profile. Give 7 questions as cards (meta = what it tests · who usually asks it) with STAR model answers drawn from the profile's level and subject, a quote with a strong answer to 'why this school', bullets of safeguarding phrasing that must be exactly right, and a checklist of questions to ask the panel.

tools.title: Build my portfolio
tools.subtitle: Evidence over adjectives
tools.prompt: Design a teaching portfolio in {format} for the profile's status and level. Provide a table (Section | Artefact to include | What it proves | Pages or slides), a checklist of artefacts to collect this term (anonymised work samples, data trackers, feedback, lesson plans), steps for assembling it in a weekend, and a callout on pupil privacy and permissions.

disclaimer: Pay-scale, contract and safeguarding information is general guidance, not legal or HR advice; follow your school, union and regulator's official policies.
